title: Audit Whether Accept-All Coding Has Cost You Ownership
summary: Sachin Kumar packages a read-only audit for Swift projects that looks for ownership-loss signals such as massive views, security shortcuts, migration theater, low-value tests, and suspicious git churn. It requires file, line, or commit evidence for every finding and produces a scored reclaim plan without modifying the code. A lead can run it before a broad cleanup and manually verify the highest-severity evidence.
takeaway: Run the audit before a broad AI-led cleanup, then manually inspect its three highest-severity findings and commit evidence; use the result to choose a narrow stabilization boundary, not an automatic rewrite.
